correctness.rationale: The ordered three-point density \(6/L^3\) leads to exact gap density \(6(L-u-v)/L^3\). The inscribed-angle theorem makes the largest angle half the maximum of the three circular gaps. Integrating the intersection \(u,v\le2m\) and complementary gap \(2\pi-u-v\le2m\) gives a direct one-dimensional cubic integral and the stated positive-part formula. The support bound follows from gap sum and the restricted angular span and is attained in closure by explicit configurations. The acute threshold and all four lower-tail coefficients are direct exact polynomial expansions. The standalone checker independently implements the gap integral and sampling and passed; finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Restricting visible circumference is a canonical geometric-sampling deformation of the classical complete-circle triangle model. The theorem solves the full family exactly, classifies which arc lengths permit acute triangles, gives a strict acute-probability law, and identifies a non-obvious codimension-one critical aperture \(4\pi/3\) at which the optimal-angle lower tail changes exponent from two to three. This is a natural complete classification and sharp phase transition, not a renaming or arbitrary numerical cutoff; its proof identifies the contributing gap geometry.
